title: Who’s Deciding Your AI Marketing Future?
summary: AI is changing B2B marketing organizations. Leaders can define the organization they intend to create, or they can leave it to hundreds of decisions about tools, workflows, and automation that collectively define the future organization for them. The key is to drive adoption toward an intended future while also encouraging experimentation for new learning.
body_markdown:
Imagine a B2B company where a field marketing manager puts an AI agent to work for them. They give it a goal to help plan regional programs and draft event invitations. They provide it with access to CRM records, marketing engagement data, past program results, and approved messaging. The field marketing manager reviews the agent’s recommendations, adds what they know about account priorities and sales relationships, and decides which programs to run and prospect contacts to target.


The field marketing manager chalks this up as a “win.” Their preparation got faster. Prospects were engaged and salespeople gained some good opportunities. The early productivity gain was real. The initial pilot worked. And so they continue to use the agent and check its actions less and less often, until they leave it to run autonomously.


Now, imagine the agent is missing changes to the targeting context. Buying groups in certain priority accounts have now reached a stage (e.g., evaluate or commit) where certain program tactics aren’t relevant or consider an account team that is trying to resolve a sensitive customer issue at one of the target accounts, but the agent has no visibility into this. Without additional information, the agent continues to send event registrations to contacts from these target accounts.


Target account activity is increasing, but the programs are not hitting the mark for all account needs. Worse yet, some agent-led activities now risk creating friction with prospects and customer relationships. With no one reviewing the agent’s decisions and actions, these mismatches (and others) can continue. And when human judgment is removed from the process in the name of agent-driven productivity, no one may notice until the opt-out requests and negative responses start hitting the sales team.


## **When Short-Term AI Decisions Become Long-Term Constraints**


In the field marketing example, faster preparation justified giving AI more autonomy and initial positive results led to more autonomy that allowed the marketer to move on from reviewing its output. This, in turn, enabled the marketer to reallocate their time for other responsibilities. What’s more, t


he productivity gain may have also suggested to management that they could make do with a smaller team.


Now consider this scenario playing out across further individual-contributor-led scenarios. The risk quickly goes beyond a single individual making customer-impacting decisions, removing human judgment and oversight to a collection of decisions that unintentionally define the marketing organization of the future.


Said another way, the search for easy productivity gains resulted in decisions that leadership did not deliberately choose. And when it is difficult or impossible to unwind such decisions and restore the previous team structure and processes, the “wins” can drive a new way of working and fundamentally alter the trajectory of the marketing organization.


But such a future wasn’t inevitable. The leadership lesson is to avoid treating near-term success as automatic permission for expanding use cases while still encouraging testing and experimentation.


## **Intentionally Define Your AI-Enabled Future**


AI is changing B2B marketing organizations. There’s no doubt about that. Leaders can define the organization they intend to become and direct AI adoption strategy toward it, or they can leave it to potentially hundreds of decisions about tools, workflows, and automation that collectively define the organization for them. The choice is whether AI changes marketing to enable the future you intend or if you allow an “unchosen future” to become the default.
